question: Who was the first president of BCCI?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**RE Grant Govan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RE Grant Govan** was the first president of the **Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).**
 
• The **BCCI** was established in **1928** as the governing body for cricket in India.
 
• **RE Grant Govan** was a British businessman, and his involvement with cricket in India marked the beginning of organized cricket administration in the country.
 
• Under his presidency, the BCCI became affiliated with the **Imperial Cricket Conference** (now the International Cricket Council or ICC), allowing Indian cricket to participate in international events.
 
• He played a pivotal role in laying the foundation for the development and governance of cricket in India during the colonial era.
 
• His tenure as the first president marked the transition of cricket administration in India from informal setups to a structured organization.
 
• The establishment of the BCCI under his leadership created the framework for the advancement of cricket, making India a significant player in global cricket over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Sikandar Hayat Khan**__

 __
 
• Sikandar Hayat Khan was a prominent **politician** and leader in British India, especially in the region of Punjab.
 
• He served as the **Premier of the Punjab** during the British era but had no significant connection with cricket or the BCCI.
 
• His contributions were primarily in the realm of politics and governance rather than sports administration.
 
 
 
• ** AN Ghose**__
 __
 
• AN Ghose was not associated with the establishment or early governance of the **BCCI**.
 
• There is no historical record of AN Ghose being involved in cricket administration, making this option incorrect in the context of the question.
 
 
 
• ** PM Rungta**__
 
 
• PM Rungta was a notable cricket administrator in India, but his involvement came later in the history of the BCCI.
 
• He served as **BCCI President** during the 1960s, several decades after the organization was established.
 
• His contributions were significant in advancing Indian cricket, but he was not the first president of the BCCI.
